variants.name: Format
variants.msg: token format invalid: expected 'claims.hmac', got {0} '.'-separated parts

variants.name: InvalidSignature
variants.msg: HMAC verification failed (tampered or wrong key)

variants.name: Jwt
variants.doc: Covers signature mismatch, malformed token, expired `exp`, wrong algorithm. `jsonwebtoken` collapses these into one error type with a `.kind()` discriminator — the Display impl is descriptive enough for logs. A caller that needs to distinguish "expired" from "bad signature" (e.g., to return a different gRPC status detail) can downcast via `.kind()`.

variants.name: KeyEncoding
variants.msg: ed25519 signing key → PKCS#8 DER encoding failed (corrupt key?): {0}
variants.doc: Signing key → PKCS#8 DER encoding. Only reachable from [`sign`] (verify uses raw pubkey bytes). Never fails for a valid ed25519 key — it's a fixed-format serialization — so this variant firing means the key itself is corrupt. Kept as a variant rather than `.expect()` because key material comes from outside (K8s Secret) and a corrupt mount should error cleanly, not panic the gateway.

variants.name: Cancelled
variants.doc: Cancel flag observed before the per-build cgroup exists. I-166: distinct from the post-cgroup path (cgroup.kill → the sandboxed build is killed and the executor reports the cancellation) so `is_infra_transient` doesn't retry it. `spawn_build_task` maps any `Err` with `cancelled=true` to `BuildResultStatus::Cancelled` regardless of variant; this variant just makes the pre-cgroup abort explicit in logs.

variants.name: CgroupOom
variants.msg: cgroup OOM during build; bumping resource floor
variants.doc: Pod-level cgroup `memory.events` `oom_kill` incremented during the build. The kernel killed a build process (cc1, ld, …) for hitting `memory.max`; make typically respawns it → OOM-loop that never converges (I-196). Distinct from `BuildFailed` because the derivation isn't broken — this builder is undersized. Maps to `InfrastructureFailure` so the scheduler bumps the drv's `resource_floor` instead of marking it permanently failed.

variants.name: Glue
variants.msg: derivation rejected by the request glue: {0}
variants.doc: The request glue rejected the derivation (unsupported builtin, malformed structuredAttrs, exportReferencesGraph outside the closure, …). Per `GlueError`'s contract these are all input problems — deterministic per-derivation, so they map to `InputRejected` (see [`ExecutorError::is_permanent`]) instead of burning fleet retries.

variants.name: InvalidDerivation
variants.doc: The assignment's `.drv` content is malformed (UTF-8, ATerm parse, BasicDerivation conversion). Deterministic per-derivation: every pod sees the same bytes, so retry-on-another-pod is pointless. Maps to `InputRejected` instead of `InfrastructureFailure`.

variants.name: SandboxSetup
variants.doc: The native sandbox failed to set up (host-side skeleton build, fork/pipe plumbing, or an in-child setup phase reported over the status pipe). The build itself never ran. Worker-local and usually transient (FS race, FUSE hiccup while bind-mounting an input) — retried locally a bounded number of times before the failure escalates to the scheduler.

variants.name: WrongKind
variants.msg: wrong executor kind: derivation is_fod={is_fod} but this executor is {executor_kind:?}

variants.name: InvalidBuildId
variants.msg: invalid build_id {0:?}: must be non-empty and contain no '/' or NUL

variants.name: SameFilesystem
variants.msg: overlay upper ({upper}) and FUSE lower ({lower}) are on the same filesystem (st_dev={st_dev}); the kernel will reject this mount. Set --overlay-base-dir to a directory on a different mount (e.g., a local SSD emptyDir volume, not the FUSE mount).

variants.name: UpperOnOverlayfs
variants.msg: overlay upperdir {path} is itself on an overlayfs mount (statfs f_type=OVERLAYFS_SUPER_MAGIC); the kernel refuses to use an overlayfs as upperdir/workdir. Set --overlay-base-dir to a directory on a real filesystem (e.g., a local SSD emptyDir volume), not the merged view of another overlay.

variants.name: InvalidReference
variants.msg: unparseable store path in recorded references: {path:?}
variants.doc: A reference recorded by the result pipeline fails `StorePath::parse`. The pipeline resolves references against validated input-closure and output paths, so this indicates a bug upstream (or a mismatched store-prefix). Surfaced as an error — silently dropping the ref would publish a path with a broken reference graph.

variants.name: Empty
variants.doc: Input was empty or contained only whitespace after trimming.

variants.name: InteriorWhitespace
variants.doc: Input contained whitespace between non-whitespace characters (e.g., `"team a"` — probably a misconfigured `authorized_keys` comment with a space where a dash was intended). Carries the trimmed input for the error message so the operator sees exactly what was rejected.

variants.name: Finalizer
variants.doc: finalizer() wrapper failed. Inner is either our own Error (ApplyFailed/CleanupFailed wrapping the reconcile body's error) or a finalizer-specific failure (couldn't patch metadata.finalizers).

variants.name: InvalidSpec
variants.doc: Failed to build a K8s object (Job, PodSpec) from the CRD spec. Usually a bad Quantity string (fuseCacheSize that doesn't parse) or some spec field we can't translate. These are OPERATOR errors — fix the CRD and reconcile retries. Not transient.

variants.name: Kube
variants.doc: K8s API error (connection, permission, not-found).

variants.name: InvalidRequest
variants.doc: The request failed [`ExecutionRequest::validate`]. The message names the rule that was violated and the offending path or field.

variants.name: Setup
variants.doc: The forked process reported a sandbox-setup failure before reaching `execve`. Carries the failing phase, the errno, and (for indexed phases such as bind mounts) which entry failed.

variants.name: Skeleton
variants.msg: failed to build the sandbox skeleton: {0}
variants.doc: Building the host-side chroot skeleton failed (directory creation, the synthesized `/etc` files, inline files, or the per-bind source stat).

variants.name: Spawn
variants.doc: Creating the supervision plumbing failed: pipes, the pty, the fork itself, the cgroup attach, or the go signal.

variants.name: ClientReported
variants.doc: Error already reported to the client via `STDERR_ERROR`. Produced by the `stderr_err!` macro — the message was shown to the client and this error terminates the session.

variants.name: DerivationNotFound
variants.doc: Derivation lookup failed.

variants.name: DerivationParse
variants.doc: Derivation ATerm parse failed.

variants.name: DrvCacheFull
variants.msg: per-session derivation cache full ({count} entries, cap {cap})
variants.doc: Per-session drv cache at cap.

variants.name: GrpcStream
variants.doc: gRPC stream/channel error (channel closed, task panicked).

variants.name: InvalidPathInfo
variants.doc: PathInfo validation rejected wire input.

variants.name: InvalidReference
variants.doc: Invalid reference path in a reference list.

variants.name: InvalidStorePath
variants.doc: Invalid store path from wire input.

variants.name: NarRead
variants.doc: NAR read error (short read, IO error).

variants.name: NarTooLarge
variants.doc: NAR size exceeds configured limit.

variants.name: Scheduler
variants.doc: gRPC call to rio-scheduler failed.

variants.name: SchedulerRejected
variants.doc: The scheduler VALIDATED the submission and refused it (`INVALID_ARGUMENT` / `FAILED_PRECONDITION`). Unlike [`GatewayError::Scheduler`] this is not infrastructure trouble: retrying the identical submission can never succeed, so callers that convert errors into `BuildResult`s must report `InputRejected`, never `TransientFailure`.

variants.name: Store
variants.doc: gRPC call to rio-store failed.

variants.name: UnknownOpcode
variants.msg: unknown opcode {0}, closing connection to avoid stream desynchronization
variants.doc: Client sent an opcode we don't recognize. Connection must close to avoid stream desync (the payload shape is unknown).

variants.name: EofWithoutTerminal
variants.msg: build event stream ended unexpectedly (scheduler disconnected?)
variants.doc: Stream returned `Ok(None)` (EOF) without a Completed/ Failed/Cancelled event. This IS the primary failover signature: k8s pod kill → SIGTERM → graceful shutdown → TCP FIN → clean stream close. NOT a Transport error. Reconnect-worthy for the same reason as Transport.

variants.name: Transport
variants.doc: gRPC-level error (connection reset, timeout). Scheduler may have failed over — reconnecting via WatchBuild has a good chance of resuming.

variants.name: Wire
variants.doc: Error writing STDERR to the client (WireError). The Nix client disconnected or the SSH channel closed. NOT reconnect-worthy — scheduler is fine, client is gone.

variants.name: CycleDetected
variants.msg: cycle detected in derivation graph at: {0}

variants.name: FixedOutputNoPath
variants.msg: bad path '' in derivation (fixed output '{0}' must specify its output path)

variants.name: FloatingCaDeclaredPath
variants.msg: content-addressing derivation output should not specify output path (output '{0}')

variants.name: HashWithoutAlgo
variants.msg: derivation output '{0}' specifies a hash without outputHashAlgo (the reference parser silently drops such hashes on unparse, breaking byte-faithful round-trips)

variants.name: InvalidUtf8
variants.msg: derivation content is not valid UTF-8: {0}

variants.name: NoOutputs
variants.msg: derivation must have at least one output

variants.name: NonDeferredFill
variants.msg: internal: fill_deferred refused non-deferred output '{0}' (deferred-filter/fill drift — report this)

variants.name: NotInputAddressed
variants.msg: derivation '{0}' is not plain input-addressed (fixed-output and floating-CA outputs derive their paths from content, not from the derivation hash)

variants.name: DuplicateOutputName
variants.doc: Two outputs share a name. The oracle's eval refuses to construct this set (primops.cc:1529, wording verbatim); its parsers would first-wins-collapse it (module doc, divergence 4) — rio rejects fail-closed so name-keyed views stay total.

variants.name: FixedNotNamedOut
variants.msg: single fixed output must be named "out"
variants.doc: The single fixed output is not named "out".

variants.name: FloatingAlgoMismatch
variants.msg: all floating outputs must use the same hash algorithm
variants.doc: Floating outputs disagree on the hash algorithm (compared after stripping the `r:` method prefix — method is not part of the oracle's `hashAlgo`).

variants.name: Mixed
variants.doc: Outputs of different kinds in one derivation (including concrete-IA mixed with deferred-IA — distinct types in the oracle's `decide`).

variants.name: MultipleFixed
variants.msg: only one fixed output is allowed for now
variants.doc: More than one fixed output.

variants.name: NoOutputs
variants.msg: must have at least one output
variants.doc: Empty output set.

variants.name: EmptyOutputName
variants.msg: output name must not be empty

variants.name: NotDerivation
variants.msg: built path base must be a derivation (.drv): {0}

variants.name: VersionTooOld
variants.msg: client protocol version {client_major}.{client_minor} is too old; rio-build requires 1.35+

variants.name: WrongDigestLength
variants.msg: wrong digest length for {algo}: expected {expected}, got {got}

variants.name: WrongEncodedLength
variants.msg: hash {hash:?} has wrong length {len} for hash algorithm '{algo}': expected {b16} (base16), {b32} (nixbase32), or {b64} (base64) characters

variants.name: InvalidUtf8
variants.msg: invalid UTF-8 in {context} at byte offset {offset}

variants.name: UnsortedEntries
variants.msg: directory entries not in sorted order: {prev:?} >= {cur:?}

variants.name: UnsupportedFileType
variants.msg: file {0:?} has an unsupported type (not regular/symlink/directory)

variants.name: LengthMismatch
variants.msg: rewrite pair {index}: from is {from} bytes but to is {to} bytes (must be equal)

variants.name: FixedOutputRefsNotAllowed
variants.msg: fixed-output path with references or self-reference requires recursive SHA-256 (got {algo}, recursive={recursive})

variants.name: InvalidBase32Padding
variants.msg: invalid nixbase32 string: non-zero padding bits (non-canonical encoding)

variants.name: TooShort
variants.msg: path is too short to contain a hash

variants.name: MalformedJson
variants.doc: `__json` is present but does not parse — the derivation claims structured attrs and the claim is unreadable. Fail-closed consumers MUST NOT degrade this to "attr absent" (the pre-fix readers did, which let an unparseable blob neutralize every behavioral attribute at once).

variants.name: WrongType
variants.doc: The attribute exists in the parsed blob with the wrong type. Mirrors the oracle's `e.addTrace(... "while parsing attribute \"%s\"")` framing around its `get*` throw.

variants.name: NotStringOrArray
variants.msg: value is not an array or a string: {dump}
variants.doc: Oracle `flatten` (derivation-options.cc:106-114).

variants.name: NotUnsigned
variants.msg: Expected JSON value to be an unsigned integral number but it is of type '{got}': {dump}
variants.doc: Oracle `getUnsigned` (json-utils.cc:62-73) — kept distinct because its message names the refined numeric storage class. Raised here only for non-numbers (see [`unsigned_lossy`]).

variants.name: WrongType
variants.msg: Expected JSON value to be of type '{want}' but it is of type '{got}': {dump}
variants.doc: Oracle `ensureType` (json-utils.cc:35-45).

variants.name: FrameTooLarge
variants.msg: framed stream frame size {0} exceeds maximum {MAX_FRAME_SIZE}

variants.name: FramedStreamTooLarge
variants.msg: framed stream total size {0} exceeds maximum {MAX_FRAMED_TOTAL}

variants.name: Io
variants.doc: Spool write failure ([`collect_nar_stream_to_writer`] only). NOT transient — retrying the gRPC won't fix local disk.

variants.name: MissingDbId
variants.msg: merge persistence references an unpersisted derivation (db_id missing): {drv_path}
variants.doc: Invariant violation: merge persistence needed a derivation's `db_id` and none exists. Two producers: the build→derivation link loop (a node this submission merely joins should have had its `db_id` committed by the merge that created it) and edge endpoint resolution (id_map for rows this merge wrote, the live DAG for everything else). Either way the node was never part of a committed submission (malformed request) or the resolution logic has a bug.

variants.name: NotLeader
variants.doc: `r[sched.lease.standby-drops-writes]`: the actor dequeued a state-writing command after losing the lease. Maps to gRPC UNAVAILABLE (same string as the gRPC layer's `ensure_leader`) so BalancedChannel clients retry against the new leader.

variants.name: PermissionDenied
variants.msg: permission denied: build {build_id} belongs to a different tenant
variants.doc: `r[sched.tenant.authz]`: caller's attested `claims.sub` does not own the build. Maps to gRPC PERMISSION_DENIED.

variants.name: SettledConflictEvidenceBudget
variants.msg: the per-merge store-evidence budget was exhausted before the settled conflict for {drv_path} could be verified; split the submission into smaller batches or retry after earlier conflicts resolve
variants.doc: `r[sched.merge.store-evidence-displacement+1]`: the per-merge store-evidence fetch budget was exhausted before this settled conflict could be verified. Maps to RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED with actionable guidance (split the submission); partial displacements from earlier conflicts in the SAME submission are not persisted — the merge is atomic (`sched.persist.atomic-activation`).

variants.name: SettledConflictEvidenceUnavailable
variants.msg: store evidence unavailable ({reason}) while resolving a settled identity conflict for {drv_path}; retry when the store recovers
variants.doc: `r[sched.merge.store-evidence-displacement+1]`: a settled-conflict resolution needed store evidence and the store stayed SILENT (fetch failure, absent path, transport-grade noise). TRANSIENT: maps to UNAVAILABLE so clients retry when the store recovers — silence must never harden into the permanent FAILED_PRECONDITION the conflict itself would carry.

variants.name: SettledIdentityConflict
variants.msg: derivation {drv_path} has a settled (successfully built) record with a different identity; re-creating it would erase that record. {remediation}
variants.doc: `r[sched.persist.settled-identity-freeze+1]`: a submission tried to (re)create a derivation whose persisted row is SETTLED (completed/skipped — the durable record of a successful build, possibly already reaped from the DAG) under a conflicting identity. Maps to FAILED_PRECONDITION (client-actionable conflict). The `remediation` is GENERATED from the arbitration verdict's refuse arm (`sched.merge.store-evidence-displacement+1`, fix-discipline R6) — a refused class structurally cannot emit a remediation its verdict does not support.

variants.name: StoreEvidenceContradicts
variants.msg: the store derivation at {drv_path} contradicts this submission's claimed identity; the declared outputs/flags do not derive from the .drv bytes the store holds at that path
variants.doc: `r[sched.merge.store-evidence-displacement+1]`: the merge-time store-evidence check fetched the `.drv` the submission's declared `drv_path` names, verified its text content-address, and the parsed derivation CONTRADICTS the submission's claimed identity — the store, not the prior record, disproves the claim. Maps to FAILED_PRECONDITION: the submitter's declared identity does not belong to the derivation at that path, so no retry of the same claim can succeed (fix the submission, or the `.drv` upload it references).

variants.name: StoreUnavailable
variants.msg: store service unavailable (cache-check circuit breaker open)
variants.doc: Store service is unreachable (cache-check circuit breaker is open). Maps to gRPC UNAVAILABLE. Rejecting SubmitBuild here is the user decision from phase2c planning: if the store is down, builds can't dispatch anyway (workers PutPath/GetPath also fail), so fail fast with a clear error instead of queueing builds that will all stall.

variants.name: AuthoritativeClaimIdentityConflict
variants.msg: authoritative inline content for {drv_path} conflicts with the existing store-backed derivation definition (no matching content-bound identity evidence); if this is your own derivation, re-upload the .drv and resubmit store-backed, ask an operator to clear the parked definition, or wait for its retention window to expire
variants.doc: The inverse direction of [`Self::ConflictingInFlightContent`]: a submission claiming authoritative inline content landed on an existing STORE-BACKED node that is eligible for the resubmit-reset, and its verifiable identity does not match the existing node's. Admitting it would let the claim redefine a parked (failed / cancelled / poison-reset) store-backed definition through the reset, carrying the prior builds' interest onto bytes only the claimant can see. An identity-matching claim is admitted through the normal resubmit-reset instead, and an authoritative claim never displaces a store-backed node. Maps to `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (client-actionable conflict, not an internal invariant breach).

variants.name: AuthoritativeContentMismatch
variants.msg: conflicting authoritative derivation content for {drv_path}: a node with different inline content already exists
variants.doc: A submission claimed authoritative inline derivation content for a node that already holds DIFFERENT authoritative content. Those bytes are the only copy of their derivation anywhere, so silently joining would let the second submitter redefine what the first one's build runs and what recovery rebuilds. Returned while the existing claim is live or `Failed` (still owned by the retry machinery — `RefusedInFlight`), or settled with a definition- evidence rank ≥ the displacer's (`RefusedSettledOutranked`; authoritative displacers carry `content_bound_claim`, so a settled authoritative claim is never redefined by another authoritative claim) — once it parks in a terminal failure state the byte-different submission displaces it instead of being rejected. Maps to `FAILED_PRECONDITION` (client-actionable conflict, not an internal invariant breach).

variants.name: ConflictingInFlightContent
variants.msg: derivation {drv_path} carries authoritative inline content that conflicts with this submission's declared identity; if the existing record is a squat on your derivation's path, upload your .drv to the store and resubmit store-backed — the scheduler verifies the store derivation and displaces the squat
variants.doc: A store-backed (non-authoritative) submission's verifiable identity (system, output names, fixed-output flag, content-addressed flag, declared expected output paths, plus content-bound evidence — a shared fixed-output path or a matching CA modular hash) conflicts with a node that carries authoritative inline content and is either still in flight or settled without being strictly outranked. Joining would attribute that node's results to a derivation that either provably differs or cannot be shown to be the same; erasing a settled (Completed/Skipped) record takes STRICTLY higher definition evidence than the settled node's rank (`sched.merge.evidence-ranked-displacement`) — a bare store-backed echo (`unverified_claim`) never qualifies, while an ingress-byte-bound submission (`path_bound_bytes`) displaces a content-bound squat. Maps to `FAILED_PRECONDITION`; once the conflicting node sits in a terminal FAILURE state the verifiable definition displaces it regardless of rank. (An identity-MATCHING store-backed submission never sees this error: it joins the node, or displaces it without error when the node is poison-locked — terminal failure, no longer retriable on resubmit.) A legitimate bare-resubmission claimant hitting this against a settled squat is self-service: upload the genuine `.drv` to the store and resubmit — the merge-time store-evidence check (`sched.merge.store-evidence-displacement+1`) verifies the claim against the store's text-CA-bound bytes and raises it past the squat's rank.

variants.name: Db
variants.doc: DB error from the realisations lookup or `realisation_deps` insert. Transient (PG blip) — caller should defer and retry.

variants.name: InvalidInputDrvPath
variants.msg: input derivation path is not a valid store path: {0}
variants.doc: An `inputDrvs` path didn't parse as a `StorePath`. Nix never produces this — guard against manually-crafted derivations.

variants.name: InvalidUtf8
variants.msg: derivation content is not valid UTF-8: {0}
variants.doc: The `drv_content` bytes weren't valid UTF-8. ATerm is ASCII; a non-UTF-8 blob means the gateway inlined garbage.

variants.name: NoDrvContent
variants.msg: drv_content is empty — cannot resolve without ATerm
variants.doc: No `drv_content` available. Resolution requires the full ATerm to parse `inputDrvs` and perform placeholder replacement. Caller should fetch from store or defer.

variants.name: Parse
variants.doc: ATerm parse failed. Likely a truncated or corrupted inline.

variants.name: RealisationMissing
variants.doc: A CA input's realisation wasn't found. The DAG guarantees the input is Completed before the parent dispatches (all deps must be Completed for Queued→Ready), so a missing realisation means the input completed WITHOUT registering a realisation — either `wopRegisterDrvOutput` was never called (client bug) or the realisation row was GC'd (scheduler/GC bug).

variants.name: Store
variants.doc: DB error from `rio_store::realisations::query`. Same retry-ability as [`Db`](Self::Db); separate variant only because rio-store's accessors return the SQLSTATE-classified [`MetadataError`](rio_store::error::MetadataError) rather than raw `sqlx::Error`.

variants.name: TerminalBuild
variants.msg: cannot transition from terminal build state {from:?} to {to:?}

variants.name: TerminalToNonTerminal
variants.msg: cannot transition from terminal state {from} to {to}

variants.name: Closed
variants.doc: Semaphore closed. Unreachable in production (nothing calls `Semaphore::close`); mapped so a future shutdown-close surfaces as transient retry, not panic.

variants.name: Saturated
variants.doc: Queued for [`SUBSTITUTE_ADMISSION_WAIT`] without acquiring. Transient — caller retries per `r[sched.substitute.detached+5]`.

variants.name: Corrupt
variants.msg: chunk {} failed BLAKE3 verification (corrupt; expected {}, got {})
variants.doc: BLAKE3 of the fetched bytes doesn't match the requested hash. S3 bitrot, memory corruption, or a backend bug. The corrupt bytes are NOT cached (we verify before insert).

variants.name: NotFound
variants.msg: chunk {} not found in backend (data loss if manifest claims it exists)
variants.doc: Backend returned None — chunk not in S3. If the manifest says this hash exists, this is data loss. Caller should propagate as a hard error (not retry — retrying NotFound is pointless).

variants.name: BadLength
variants.msg: manifest body length {0} is not a multiple of {ENTRY_SIZE} (truncated or corrupt)

variants.name: Conflict
variants.doc: Unique or FK constraint violation (PG codes 23505, 23503). Usually means a concurrent writer won the race — the caller's operation is a no-op, not a failure. Maps to `already_exists`.

variants.name: Connection
variants.doc: Connection-level failure: pool exhausted, TCP reset, TLS error. Retriable — the operation never reached PG. Maps to `unavailable`.

variants.name: CorruptManifest
variants.doc: A `manifest_data.chunk_list` blob failed to deserialize. Written by us, read by us — if it doesn't round-trip, either the write was torn or the format version is wrong. NOT retriable. Maps to `data_loss`.

variants.name: Deadlock
variants.doc: Deadlock detected (PG code 40P01). Two transactions have a circular lock-wait on overlapping row sets. Retriable — PG aborted one txn; retry will likely succeed. Prevention: sort batch-UPDATE input so all writers acquire locks in the same order (see `metadata::with_sorted_retry`). Maps to `aborted`.

variants.name: InvariantViolation
variants.doc: Database state violates a code-enforced invariant that PG's schema can't express (e.g., `inline_blob IS NULL` but no `manifest_data` row — PG can't CHECK "row in another table exists"). This is corruption: manual DB surgery, a CASCADE we didn't expect, or a bug in cleanup ordering. NOT retriable. Maps to `internal`.

variants.name: MalformedRow
variants.doc: A narinfo row failed validation (bad store_path, wrong-length nar_hash). PG's schema doesn't enforce these as CHECK constraints. Caught at the egress boundary. NOT retriable. Maps to `internal`.

variants.name: NotFound
variants.doc: Row not found. From `sqlx::Error::RowNotFound`. Most metadata queries use `fetch_optional` so this is rare; shows up on `fetch_one` sites.

variants.name: Other
variants.doc: Unclassified sqlx error. Maps to `internal`.

variants.name: PlaceholderMissing
variants.doc: The write-ahead placeholder from `insert_manifest_uploading` is gone — `delete_manifest_uploading` raced us and won, or a crashed previous upload already cleaned it up. The caller's UPDATE hit `rows_affected() == 0`. Retriable. Maps to `aborted`.

variants.name: RealisationConflict
variants.msg: realisation conflict: ({drv_hash}, {output_name}) already maps to {existing}, attempted {attempted}
variants.doc: `realisations` insert hit `(drv_hash, output_name)` PK with a DIFFERENT `output_path` than the existing row. CA derivations are deterministic — same key, same output — so this means either a determinism bug or an attempted poison (pre-register `(public_hash → /nix/store/EVIL)`). NOT silently swallowed by `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`. Maps to `already_exists` + WARN.

variants.name: ResourceExhausted
variants.doc: Backpressure / quota exhaustion: PG pool timeout under load, signature count cap, or similar capacity conditions. Maps to `resource_exhausted`. Pool-timeout: retriable (transient). Sig-cap: per-path permanent — the UPDATE already committed and `DISTINCT` dedup means retry hits the same cardinality>cap forever (closer to `FAILED_PRECONDITION` semantics, but mapped here for now). Distinct from [`Connection`](Self::Connection): that's "PG unreachable" (connect failed, TCP reset, TLS error); this is "PG reachable but at capacity" (pool timed out waiting for a free connection). The gRPC code is different — `unavailable` tells clients to try another replica; `resource_exhausted` tells them to back off.

variants.name: Serialization
variants.doc: Serialization failure (PG code 40001). Two transactions conflicted under REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE isolation. Retriable — the transaction was aborted cleanly, retry will likely succeed. Maps to `aborted`.

variants.name: Format
variants.msg: key file format: expected 'name:base64', got {0} ':'-separated parts

variants.name: KeyLength
variants.msg: secret key must be 32 or 64 bytes, got {0}
variants.doc: Nix's format is 64 bytes (seed + pubkey). We also accept just the 32-byte seed. Anything else is malformed.

variants.name: TenantKeyLookup
variants.doc: DB lookup of a tenant's signing key failed. Stringified `MetadataError` — `metadata` is `pub(crate)`, so we can't put the typed error on a `pub` signature. The distinction between retriable (Connection) and permanent (InvariantViolation) is lost here; callers that care should hit `metadata::get_active_signer` directly. The cluster-key fallback (`tenant_id = None`) never touches the DB, so it never hits this variant.

variants.name: Admission
variants.doc: Per-replica admission gate timed out (or closed). Transient — `Err` so moka does NOT cache it; the next caller after the burst clears retries cleanly.

variants.name: Fetch
variants.doc: Upstream HTTP request failed (connect, TLS, 5xx). The upstream URL is folded into the message for operator-side debugging.

variants.name: HashMismatch
variants.doc: The ingested NAR's SHA-256 didn't match the narinfo's `NarHash:` line. Upstream served corrupt bytes (or lied in the narinfo).

variants.name: Ingest
variants.doc: Metadata-layer failure during ingest (write-ahead, complete_manifest, chunked S3/refcount).

variants.name: NarInfo
variants.doc: narinfo parse failed, or the `NarHash:` line didn't decode to a 32-byte SHA-256. Upstream served garbage.

variants.name: Raced
variants.doc: Transient placeholder-claim: another uploader holds the slot. Same-replica `try_substitute*` callers coalesce at the moka `inflight` singleflight and never reach `claim_placeholder` concurrently, so this only surfaces on **cross-replica** races (another rio-store pod) or a concurrent `PutPath`. Returned as `Err` (not `Ok(None)`) so moka does NOT cache it; the caller's retry re-runs `do_substitute` and reaches `AlreadyComplete` once the in-flight upload lands. gRPC maps to `NotFound` (the gateway's 2-attempt budget can't outlast a multi-second NAR fetch, so callers re-probe later).

variants.name: RateLimited
variants.doc: Transient upstream-429 (`r[store.substitute.probe-429-retry+2]`). `retry_after` is the parsed `Retry-After` header (delta-seconds or HTTP-date), `None` if absent or unparseable. Returned as `Err` so moka does NOT cache it; the admission permit is dropped on return so the wait happens caller-side without holding per-replica capacity. gRPC maps to `Unavailable` so the scheduler's 8-attempt backoff retries — a bare 429 (no `Retry-After`) is still a real rate-limit, NOT a miss.

variants.name: SizeMismatch
variants.msg: NAR size mismatch: narinfo declared {declared}, got {actual} decompressed bytes
variants.doc: Decompressed NAR length differed from the narinfo's `NarSize:` line. Upstream lied; the Nix signature fingerprint includes `nar_size`, so persisting an unchecked size would store a row whose own signatures don't verify.

variants.name: TooLarge
variants.doc: An upstream-supplied body exceeded a size cap (narinfo, `/nix-cache-info`, declared `NarSize`, or decompressed NAR). `tenant_upstreams` rows are tenant-supplied; one tenant's hostile upstream must not OOM the process-global substituter.

enums.name: ExecutorError
enums.doc: Error type for executor operations. No `#[from] anyhow::Error` — every variant has a typed source. A catch-all `#[from] anyhow::Error` would mean any `?` on an anyhow::Result anywhere in execute_build silently becomes the wrong variant. Typed sources make the compiler catch misattribution at the `?` site.

enums.name: FetchError
enums.doc: Closed permanence classification for one fetch attempt. Every failure source inside [`try_fetch_one`] must choose a class at the point where the error is produced — there is deliberately no `From<anyhow::Error>` impl and no default bucket, so a future failure source cannot silently inherit retryability (the downcast-marker shape this replaces let exactly that happen: any error NOT carrying the marker was retryable by omission). The retry loop matches exhaustively.

enums.name: OverlayError
enums.doc: Errors from overlay setup and teardown. Distinct from `anyhow::Error` so `ExecutorError::Overlay(#[from])` only catches overlay failures — a bare `?` on an unrelated `anyhow::Result` elsewhere in `execute_build` no longer silently becomes an "overlay setup failed" message.

enums.name: UploadError
enums.doc: Errors from upload operations. NAR serialization happens inside the retry loop (each retry is a fresh disk read), so NAR errors surface as `UploadExhausted` wrapping a `tonic::Status::internal("NAR serialization failed...")`.

enums.name: NameError
enums.doc: Construction-time rejection. The `Display` impl's message is what callers map to `Status::invalid_argument`.

enums.name: Error
enums.doc: Top-level reconcile error. kube's `Controller::run` takes an `error_policy` fn that receives this and decides requeue timing. `Box` on the finalizer variant: `finalizer::Error<Self>` is recursive (it wraps our Error for ApplyFailed/CleanupFailed). Unboxed it's an infinite-size type. Box breaks the cycle with a pointer indirection.

enums.name: ExecError
enums.doc: Errors produced by the executor. Every variant is an *infrastructure* failure from the caller's point of view — a request that could not be validated or a sandbox that could not be constructed or supervised. A process that runs and exits non-zero (or is killed by a limit) is **not** an error; that is an [`ExitOutcome`] in a successful [`ExecutionOutcome`].

enums.name: GatewayError
enums.doc: Typed errors for the handler layer. Converts to `anyhow::Error` at the boundary via `thiserror`'s `std::error::Error` impl + anyhow's blanket `From<E: Error>`. The outer handler signature remains `anyhow::Result<()>` — use `.into()` or `?` to convert.

enums.name: StreamProcessError
enums.doc: Error from `process_build_events`. Distinguishes transport errors and stream EOF-without-terminal (both reconnect-worthy failover signatures — see the per-variant docs) from `Wire` (client-side disconnect — not retried).

enums.name: DerivationError
enums.doc: Errors from parsing or hashing ATerm derivations.

enums.name: DerivationTypeError
enums.doc: Ill-typed output sets, with the oracle's verbatim wording.

enums.name: DerivedPathError
enums.doc: Errors from parsing a `DerivedPath` string.

enums.name: HandshakeError
enums.doc: Errors specific to the handshake.

enums.name: NarError
enums.doc: Errors from NAR operations.

enums.name: NarInfoError
enums.doc: Errors from narinfo parsing.

enums.name: RewriteError
enums.doc: Error constructing a [`RewritingSink`] or [`HashModuloSink`].

enums.name: StructuredAttrError
enums.doc: A typed structured-attrs read failed.

enums.name: TypedError
enums.doc: A typed read failed: the value exists but is not the expected type.

enums.name: NarCollectError
enums.doc: Error from [`collect_nar_stream`] / [`collect_nar_stream_to_writer`].

enums.name: ActorError
enums.doc: Errors from the actor.

enums.name: DagError
enums.doc: Errors from DAG operations.

enums.name: ResolveError
enums.doc: Errors during CA input resolution.

enums.name: TransitionError
enums.doc: Errors from state machine transitions. Lives in mod.rs (not derivation.rs or build.rs) because variants reference both `DerivationStatus` and `BuildState` — putting it in either submodule would create a dependency on the other.

enums.name: AdmissionError
enums.doc: Domain error from [`AdmissionGate::acquire_bounded`]. Kept tonic-free so [`crate::substitute::Substituter`] can hold the gate without pulling gRPC types into its error enum; the gRPC layer maps via `From<AdmissionError> for Status`.

enums.name: ChunkError
enums.doc: Error from `ChunkCache::get_verified`.

enums.name: MetadataError
enums.doc: Typed error for the metadata/DB layer. Replaces `anyhow::Result` so callers can discriminate retriable failures (connection, serialization) from permanent ones (corruption) and map to precise gRPC status codes.

enums.name: PersistError
enums.doc: How [`persist_nar`] failed. The caller maps this to its own error domain (`tonic::Status` for gRPC, `SubstituteError` for substitution) and decides whether to [`abort_placeholder`]: the chunked path already rolled back internally.

enums.name: SubstituteError
enums.doc: Errors surfaced by the substitution path. Callers map these to gRPC status; `NotFound` is the normal miss case (no upstream has the path, or the tenant has no upstreams configured). `Clone` so moka's `try_get_with` can hand the same error to every coalesced waiter (it stores `Arc<E>` internally; we unwrap to owned).
